text:
Thomas Chabot became Ottawa's 11th captain this fall, after Brady Tkachuk was traded to Florida. He left the Oct. 17 game in Philadelphia with an upper-body injury and missed four games, but since coming back he has been productive: 7 points in his last ten games, 6 of them assists.

For the season he has 11 points in 17 games while playing 23:45 a night, a scoring rate of 1.63 points per 60 minutes, well above the league's typical defenseman at 1.1. Ottawa has taken 56.8% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, a measure of who gets the better chances. Some of the point total is luck: the Senators have scored 6.7 more goals than those chances deserve while he plays.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.0 wins above replacement last season, 29th among 215 defensemen, mostly from even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the other half of his game: he stops 16% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%, and joins the rush more than most defensemen. So far, the captaincy suits him.
headline: Chabot's first season with the C is a good one
